primary_claim: Contrary to the hypothesis that recurrence itself would let Mamba outperform Transformers at a toy hidden-serial-reasoning task, standard Mamba (whose SSM recurrence transforms each channel independently) cannot solve the hidden task at all, while a modified Mamba SSM enabling cross-channel communication can; non-linearity is not required for hidden reasoning; and Transformers need roughly 3 extra layers to gain 1 extra unit of serial computation depth.

effect.value: standard Mamba fails to solve the hidden task; a modified Mamba with cross-channel SSM communication solves it; Transformers require about +3 layers per +1 unit of solvable task length

contradicts_or_qualifies: Qualifies the assumption that recurrent architectures (like Mamba) inherently enable hidden serial reasoning by virtue of being recurrent — only recurrence with cross-channel interaction does
stated_future_work: More thorough experiments are needed to confirm whether steganography requires the model to intentionally, non-myopically hide information
limitations_stated: Even with limited-serial-depth architectures, models could still reason steganographically
Many sneaky actions (e.g. noticing an exfiltration opportunity, hiding a lie) don't require complex planning, so limiting serial depth wouldn't prevent them
With longer training the layers-per-task-length result would probably improve; results may be limited by training budget even though a million examples per tiny model was already used
quote: Not every recurrence though - connections between channels are needed. Notably Mamba architecture isn't capable of hidden reasoning.
